summary: The candidate is correct and complete. Strict envelope separation follows from half-metronoid depth, the base halfspace balance, and strict separation of the complementary base support. LP duality supplies every exact affine minorant, complementary slackness gives contact on vertex supports, and the centerpoint construction makes each affine-independent contact packet admissible for G; the one-point augmentation bound and its G<W/2 consequence are used with the correct constants. In the empty-complement branch, Farkas multipliers yield the stated nonzero negative affine-moment stress, while the induced base halfspace gives both k>a/delta and min(theta)<=eta<delta/a by unweighted and weighted covering integrals. In the nonempty-complement branch, Helly reduction, strong separation, and LP duality give the two exhaustive envelope cases; failure of the bottleneck inequality would satisfy every hypothesis of the finite-capacity selection principle and produce a reachable barycenter contradicting phi_m(u)>h_Y(u). The legal-circuit conclusion correctly uses Hausdorff convergence to a positive-volume limiting cap: volume continuity together with the outer-parallel-body squeeze gives convergence of intersection volumes, and finiteness of base traces makes the estimate uniform. The proof consistently distinguishes arbitrary exact-minorant caps from caps belonging to a support-minimal legal circuit and claims no unsupported absorption or matching conversion.
